paths.summary: Nineteen exact skill groups in four stages, with required language depth and four distinct advanced targets. Shared lessons retain one canonical record; reference results never grant your readiness.

stages.outcome: Explain the language, representation and system boundary using hand-checkable original fixtures.

groups.label: Core Languages
groups.requestedDescription: Modern C++ (pointers, manual memory, RAII, STL), Go (syntax, goroutines, structs), or Python (OOP, typing, generators).
groups.overlapNote: Python function/error/module contracts; an optional C++ port assumes rather than teaches the necessary C++ prerequisites. The commerce exercise adds typing versus validation. Required explicit C++ memory/RAII/STL and Go teaching; Python OOP/typing/generators depth. All named language branches remain taught, not discarded because the source says or.

groups.label: OS & System Calls
groups.requestedDescription: Linux process lifecycle (fork, exec, signals), file descriptors, standard I/O redirection, and POSIX debugging tools (strace, lsof, curl, netstat).
groups.overlapNote: Process identity/lifecycle and real shell streams/redirection; GATE scheduling is not a fork/exec lab. Concrete POSIX system calls, descriptor ownership and all four named diagnostic tools.

groups.label: Basic Networking & Web Protocols
groups.requestedDescription: TCP/UDP differences, 3-way handshakes, DNS resolution flow, HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2, REST API best practices, and TLS certificates.
groups.overlapNote: Framed TCP/socket reads, DNS roles, tested TLS identity failures and versioned REST contracts. Explicit TCP versus UDP behavior, three-way handshake analysis and assessed HTTP/1.1 versus HTTP/2 multiplexing/connection behavior.

groups.label: Storage Fundamentals
groups.requestedDescription: Relational database schemas, ACID transactions, B-Tree indexes, basic connection pooling, and key-value caching (Redis commands).
groups.overlapNote: Relational constraints, real PostgreSQL concurrent transactions, B/B+ tree reasoning, plan-based indexes and cache consistency contracts. Executable connection-pool lifecycle and concrete Redis command/expiry/atomicity work.

groups.label: Tooling
groups.requestedDescription: Dockerfile authoring, multi-stage builds, basic CI/CD scripting, and Git command-line hygiene (interactive rebasing, cherry-picking).
groups.overlapNote: Container packaging/runtime, CI promotion rejection and safe branch/merge history. Multi-stage Docker builds; interactive rebasing and cherry-picking in a disposable private history, never rewriting shared work.

stages.outcome: Implement and compare the named tools or protocols while preserving data, identity and lifecycle invariants.
stages.evidence: Retain actual supported-runtime integration, a bounded change and positive/negative regressions; unsupported environments remain visible.

groups.label: Safe Systems & Concurrency
groups.requestedDescription: Rust ownership, lifetimes, Arc/Mutex, Go channels/sync primitives, and thread pools.
groups.overlapNote: Generic GATE synchronization and database races are useful prerequisites, not Rust/Go language instruction. Every requested language-specific mechanism and bounded thread-pool implementation.

groups.label: Distributed RPCs & Message Brokers
groups.requestedDescription: Protocol Buffers, gRPC unary/streaming lifecycles, and Apache Kafka/RabbitMQ (partitions, consumer groups, offsets, dead-letter queues).
groups.overlapNote: Delivery, partition/key/acknowledgement and crash-boundary reasoning; no explicit gRPC or Kafka/RabbitMQ implementation lessons. Protobuf evolution and gRPC unary/client/server/bidirectional streaming; concrete Pub/Sub, Kafka and RabbitMQ consumer/offset/DLQ contracts.

groups.label: Cloud Orchestration
groups.requestedDescription: Kubernetes primitives (Deployments, StatefulSets, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets), Helm charts, and Terraform/OpenTofu infrastructure provisioning.
groups.overlapNote: Local Terraform provider/plan/state exercise, not cluster deployment or cloud provisioning. All named Kubernetes primitives, Helm packaging and paired Terraform/OpenTofu provisioning lifecycle.

groups.label: Database Optimization
groups.requestedDescription: Query execution plans (EXPLAIN ANALYZE), composite indexes, connection pool exhaustion debugging (HikariCP/pgBouncer), and optimistic locking.
groups.overlapNote: EXPLAIN ANALYZE, observed plans and composite-index trade-offs. Real HikariCP and pgBouncer exhaustion diagnosis plus optimistic version/compare-and-set locking.

groups.label: Observability
groups.requestedDescription: Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus metrics instrumentation, and structured JSON logging.
groups.overlapNote: Correlated structured telemetry, SLI arithmetic, bounded labels and privacy-safe logs; an OTel reading alone is not OTel implementation. Actual OpenTelemetry context propagation/exporters and Prometheus instruments/exposition.

stages.outcome: Diagnose failure, concurrency, resource and compatibility behavior at the actual mechanism boundary.
stages.evidence: Reproduce an original fault, repair its cause and compare against an independent oracle without substituting a simpler stack.

groups.label: Consensus & State Machine Replication
groups.requestedDescription: Implementation of Raft or Paxos protocols, write-ahead logging (WAL), snapshotting, and log compaction.
groups.overlapNote: Snapshot-plus-log recovery with integrity/version checks; not distributed consensus or a custom WAL/LSM engine. From-scratch Raft, concrete Paxos comparison/model, crash-safe WAL and consensus-aware snapshot/compaction; P1 additionally requires LSM, memtables, SSTables, Bloom filters and joint consensus.

groups.label: High-Throughput I/O
groups.requestedDescription: Asynchronous non-blocking network engines using Linux epoll/io_uring or Tokio event loops; backpressure handling.

capabilities.label: Asynchronous non-blocking network engines using Linux epoll/io_uring

groups.overlapNote: Bounded queues/deadlines and TCP framing; no event-loop implementation. All three named asynchronous I/O mechanisms with measured backpressure and cancellation.

groups.label: Service Mesh & Proxy Mechanics
groups.requestedDescription: Custom Envoy proxy configurations, reverse-proxy sidecars, token bucket rate-limiting algorithms, and circuit-breaker patterns.
groups.overlapNote: Generic retry/deadline lessons are not a reverse proxy, token bucket or circuit breaker. Envoy/sidecar configuration, independently tested rate limiting and circuit-breaking states; P2 also needs weighted routing and xDS-style gRPC control.

groups.label: Data Consistency
groups.requestedDescription: Two-Phase Commit (2PC), Saga orchestrations, distributed locks (Redlock, etcd leases), and outbox patterns with Change Data Capture (CDC).

capabilities.label: outbox patterns with Change Data Capture

groups.overlapNote: Compensation, idempotent outbox work and live-CDC assignment; commerce exercise tests fencing, not generic consensus or global exactly-once effects. Explicit 2PC versus Saga protocols and real Redlock/etcd lease caveats and fencing at protected writes.

groups.label: Kubernetes Control Plane
groups.requestedDescription: Developing custom Kubernetes Operators and Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) using controller-runtime or Kubebuilder.
groups.overlapNote: The optional existing developer CLI deliberately does not require Kubernetes. CRD schemas, controller-runtime and Kubebuilder reconciliation, status/conditions, finalizers and ownership.

stages.outcome: Defend operational, architectural and measurement decisions with evidence whose scope is explicit.
stages.evidence: Produce an owned release/incident/benchmark or decision dossier, including negative results, alternatives, actual versus modelled scale and pending hardware.

groups.label: Zero-Downtime Global Migrations
groups.requestedDescription: Large-scale distributed live database schema migrations, dual-writing proxies with shadow verification, and zero-loss cutover plans.

capabilities.label: Large-scale distributed live database schema migrations

groups.overlapNote: Backward-compatible schema evolution and local release/rollback, not a dual-writing query proxy or observed zero-loss cutover. SQL AST routing, transaction-safe dual writes, asynchronous shadow comparison, durable discrepancy window and reversible cutover.

groups.label: High-Availability System Design
groups.requestedDescription: Active-active multi-region failover, geo-replicated state machines, split-brain automated fencing, and CAP/PACELC trade-off navigation.
groups.overlapNote: Single-host recovery and worker fencing are prerequisites, not multi-region replication/failover. Every named HA design mechanism and consistency/latency trade-off.

groups.label: Mechanical Sympathy
groups.requestedDescription: CPU cache-line alignment (false sharing prevention), branch prediction optimization, and custom memory arena allocators for high-throughput microservices.

capabilities.label: custom memory arena allocators for high-throughput microservices

groups.overlapNote: GATE cache traces and optional C++ allocation discussion do not teach or assess these implementation mechanisms. False-sharing diagnosis, aligned layout, branch prediction experiments and memory arenas in a service workload.

groups.label: Platform Governance
groups.requestedDescription: Internal Developer Platform (IDP) architecture, enterprise API standards governance, cross-functional SLA/SLO definition, and cloud capacity planning.
groups.overlapNote: A bounded internal developer workflow, defined SLOs, API ownership and workload-labelled capacity/cost decisions. Enterprise IDP architecture, standards/deprecation governance and cross-functional SLA/capacity ownership at broader scope.

groups.requestedDescription: MicroVM execution runtimes (Firecracker, gVisor) for running model-generated arbitrary code securely.

capabilities.label: for running model-generated arbitrary code securely

groups.label: Ultra-Scale Multi-Node Cluster Orchestration
